spans.s:
arcā
(‘that which is worshipped’)
------------------------------------------
The Vaiṣṇavite scriptures which preach the cult of विष्णु-नारायण-कृष्ण put forth the theory that the Supreme Lord विष्णु has four kinds of manifestations:
the ‘para’ or the Supreme;
the ‘vyūha’ or the emanation;
the ‘vibhava’ or the इन्चर्नतिओन् and
the ‘arcā’ or the icon.
Out of these, the अर्चा represents the images or icons installed and worshipped ceremonially in temples and shrines. Such icons are classified into four groups: svayaṁvyakta or self-manifested, दैव or established by gods, ārṣa or consecrated by the ṛṣis (sages) and mānuṣa or prepared by human beings.
Even the man-made images, though prepared out of inanimate substances, can become ‘alive’ if they are duly consecrated through the prescribed rites. God who is omnipotent ‘descends’ into such images with a subtle body. This is the ‘arcāvatāra’ or इन्चर्नतिओन् for purposes of ordinary worship.
